data.title: Regulation of mTOR function in response to hypoxia by REDD1 and the TSC1/TSC2 tumor suppressor complex
data.authors: Brugarolas J; Lei K; Hurley RL; Manning BD; Reiling JH; Hafen E; Witters LA; Ellisen LW; Kaelin WG

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Hypoxia inhibits mTOR via REDD1-dependent activation of the TSC1/2 complex.
data.abstract_excerpt: Mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) is a central regulator of protein synthesis whose activity is modulated by a variety of signals. Energy depletion and hypoxia result in mTOR inhibition. While energy depletion inhibits mTOR through a process involving the activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) by LKB1 and subsequent phosphorylation of TSC2, the mechanism of mTOR inhibition by hypoxia is not known. Here we show that mTOR inhibition by hypoxia requires the TSC1/TSC2 tumor suppressor complex and the hypoxia-inducible gene REDD1/RTP801.

extracted_findings.effect: Hypoxia inhibits mTOR via REDD1 acting through the TSC1/TSC2 tumor-suppressor complex
